thread:
Alice: FYI canary after the continuous-batcher tuning shows p99 regression and a big drop in prefix cache hit-rate. Noticed around 03/17 21:04Z. Anyone else?

Ben: Yep, saw the same on /v1/generate. p50 steady, but p99 +~40ms and cache hit-rate fell from ~80% to ~55%. Logs hint mixed batches.

Ben: ```
2026-03-17T21:04:12Z route=/v1/generate batch_id=0x7f2a size=14 prefix_hits=6 kernel_choice=conservative_gemm latency_ms=98
2026-03-17T21:04:12Z route=/v1/generate batch_id=0x7f2b size=9  prefix_hits=3 kernel_choice=fast_gemm latency_ms=60
```

Carol: Profiling note: when batch composition mixes requests with warm KV caches and cold ones, our selector flips to a safer kernel that does extra memcopies and uses fallback kv-layout. The decision uses mean_seq_len and kv_ready_fraction thresholds. If variance within batch is high, pick conservative path.

Dylan: Remember we changed cache keyer in Feb to trim prompts to 64B + model id. That reduces identical-key matches when customers append metadata to prompts. The batching change just made that visible at scale.

Alice: Rollout timeline: keyer change 02/14, continuous-batcher tweak 03/16 23:50. Canary traffic spike triggered interaction.

Eve (perf-bot): regression_alert: canary v2.11 -> v2.12 p99 +38ms, prefix_cache_hit -25pp. trace=fb3a1.

Ben: Quick repro (low effort): spawn mixed-prefix traffic into continuous-batcher to reproduce kernel mixing.

Ben: ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 250); do
  prompt="prefix_$((i%6)) metadata:$RANDOM extra"
  curl -s -X POST http://canary/v1/generate -d \"{\\\"prompt\\\":\\\"$prompt\\\"}\" &
done
```

Carol: Experiment proposals:
- tighten affinity_window so similar prefixes are more likely to be co-batched
- introduce batch-homogenize threshold: if kv_ready_fraction_stddev > X then split batch
- metricize per-batch kernel_switch_rate and kv_ready_fraction histogram

Dylan: Also propose short-lived keyer fallback on canary: canonicalize whitespace + keep up to 256 chars (no trim) to see hit-rate impact.

Alice: Ran quick A/B with affinity_window=60ms + keyer=256chars on subset: prefix-hit jumped 56% -> 74%, p99 dropped ~30ms. Need more samples but promising.

Carol: Caution: larger keys increase cache footprint and eviction churn. Consider bumping TTL for hot prefixes or LRU biasing.

Ben: Ops asks: can we apply route-level overrides? /v1/rephrase is super latency-sensitive and seems to have low prompt variability; keep defaults there.

Dylan: Action items:
- revert continuous-batcher tweak on canary to previous params (Dylan)
- run A/B keyer test 64 vs 256 on 10% traffic (Alice)
- add per-batch logging: kv_ready_fraction, kernel_choice, prefix_hash_entropy (Carol)
- alert if prefix_hit drops >10pp or kernel_switch_rate spikes (Ben)
- create microtrace linking kernel_choice -> cache_hit outcome (Dylan)

Alice: I'll open revert PR + add A/B toggle. Assigning to @dylan and @carol for logging + microtrace. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Ben: Dashboard suggestions: kernel_switch_rate (per-route), batch_size_vs_hit_rate, kv_eviction_rate. Low-cost panels.

Carol: Slight follow-up: consider a soft-split mechanism inside batcher that separates warm-vs-cold queues at dispatch time (avoid full split but prefer homogeneous kernel paths).

Dylan: I'll prototype soft-split and add unit tests to ensure no throughput cliff.

Eve (perf-bot): note: schedule re-check in 24h.

Alice: Good plan. Let's reconvene after 24h results.
